panels.title: The fleet off the headlands
panels.desc: Defensive warships anchored in battle line along the coast; light dispatch skiffs rowing between them with signal tablets; dark hostile sails looming on the distant horizon.
panels.scene: Twilight over the coastal waters of Paxos. Four great wooden warships (triremes) ride at anchor in a wide defensive crescent off the rocky headlands, their oars half-banked and crews on alert. Between the anchored warships, slim oared dispatch skiffs skim across the choppy waters, carrying written wooden slates from ship to ship. Far out on the western horizon, the dark silhouettes of an invading enemy fleet appear against the red sunset.
panels.cast: admirals on quarterdecks, skiff crews, galley soldiers

panels.title: The anchored squadrons
panels.desc: The defensive war fleet holding its stations off the rocky coast at dusk; swift oared skiffs ply the water between flagships.
panels.scene: A wide panoramic view of the defensive fleet stationed in line of battle across the coastal bay at dusk. Each squadron flagship flies a distinct admiral's pennant from its masthead. Between the heavy galleys, swift oared skiffs row continuously along established sea lanes, delivering message slates between the admirals.
panels.caption: THE SQUADRONS RODE AT ANCHOR OFF THE COAST. THE ADMIRALS COULD CONFER ONLY BY DISPATCH SKIFFS.

panels.title: The bribed admiral
panels.desc: Inside a lamp-lit flagship cabin at night, a cloaked go-between hands an admiral a purse of foreign gold; the admiral is already dictating conflicting orders to two skiff captains at once.
panels.scene: Inside the low timber cabin of a flagship at night, illuminated by a swinging bronze oil lamp. A cloaked emissary from the invading fleet quietly passes a heavy leather purse of gold drachmas to a seated admiral. The admiral, with a cunning smile, dictates to two different dispatch scribes at once: one scribe carves a ramming-beak symbol (ATTACK) into a wax tablet, the other carves a harbor-boom symbol (FALL-BACK).
panels.cast: the bribed admiral, foreign emissary, two scribes
panels.caption: THE BRIBED ADMIRAL NEED NOT REFUSE TO FIGHT. HE NEED ONLY ORDER THE LEFT SQUADRON TO ATTACK AND THE RIGHT SQUADRON TO FALL BACK.

panels.title: Two betrayals, one view
panels.desc: A split panel: a loyal Flag Admiral betrayed by a lying lieutenant admiral, and a treacherous Flag Admiral relayed honestly — viewed from Admiral 1's quarterdeck, both appear identical.
panels.scene: A split panel with a sea-spray vertical divider. Left half: a loyal Flag Admiral sends an ATTACK tablet to Admiral 1 and the same to Admiral 2; but Admiral 2, shadowed and treacherous, sends a skiff to Admiral 1 with a forged FALL-BACK report. Right half: a traitorous Flag Admiral sends ATTACK to Admiral 1 and FALL-BACK to an honest Admiral 2, who faithfully relays FALL-BACK to Admiral 1. In both halves, Admiral 1 stands on his deck looking down at two identical conflicting slates.
panels.caption: TWO DIFFERENT BETRAYALS — AND FROM THE QUARTERDECK OF ADMIRAL 1, THEY LOOK EXACTLY ALIKE.

panels.title: The Illyrian warships
panels.desc: An admiral bends over a sea chart crowded with painted miniature wooden galleys, moving a whole cluster of them at once with both hands, like a puppeteer.
panels.scene: Inside a warship's map cabin, an admiral bends over a large painted parchment navigation chart of the coastal shoals. The chart is crowded with small painted wooden triremes representing foreign Illyrian warships. He moves a cluster of ten miniature galleys simultaneously with both hands, simulating how three admirals can play the role of an entire fleet of 3m ships.
panels.caption: EACH OF THREE ADMIRALS PLAYS THE PART OF A THIRD OF THE ENTIRE ILLYRIAN FLEET.

panels.title: The relay of the skiffs
panels.desc: Four warships anchored in coastal waters: dispatch skiffs criss-cross between them; on the deck of Warship 2, the admiral tallies three slates (two Attack, one Fall-back) to take the majority.
panels.scene: Four defensive warships anchored in a diamond formation in the coastal bay under morning sun. Four-oared dispatch skiffs criss-cross the blue water between them, wake trails spreading across the calm sea. In the foreground, on the quarterdeck of Warship 2, an admiral in a bronze breastplate sorts three wooden slates on his chart table: two read ATTACK, one reads FALL-BACK. He raises his commander's baton for ATTACK.
panels.caption: FOUR ADMIRALS, ONE TRAITOR: ADMIRAL 2 HEARS “ATTACK”, “ATTACK”, AND ONE LIE — AND OBEYS THE MAJORITY.

panels.title: The same signet, twice
panels.desc: An admiral holds two wax slates side by side in torchlight — one ordering Attack, one ordering Fall-back — both bearing the identical signet ring seal of the Flag Admiral.
panels.scene: Close-up on the quarterdeck of a warship by torchlight. An armored squadron admiral holds up two rectangular wax-coated wooden slates side-by-side: one has carved lines for ATTACK, the other for FALL-BACK. At the bottom of each slate, pressed into crimson pitch, is the exact same raised seal: the trident-and-dolphin signet ring of the Flag Admiral. The admiral stares at them, his jaw clenched.
panels.caption: THE SAME SIGNET ON TWO CONFLICTING ORDERS. ONLY THE FLAG ADMIRAL COULD HAVE STRUCK BOTH — PROVING HE IS THE TRAITOR.

panels.title: Reefs and crosscurrents
panels.desc: High bird's-eye view over the coastal sea: warships separated by treacherous shallows and reefs, where skiffs can pass only along certain deep channels through intermediate ships.
panels.scene: A dramatic bird's-eye view looking down on the coastal waters of Paxos. The defensive warships ride at anchor among jagged limestone reefs, white breaking surf, and swirling tidal whirlpools. Deep blue navigable water connects only certain pairs of warships, while others are barred by exposed rocks; dispatch skiffs must row winding routes through intermediate ships to relay their orders.
panels.caption: NOT EVERY WARSHIP COULD REACH EVERY OTHER. SOME ORDERS HAD TO ROW THROUGH OTHER ADMIRALS' SQUADRONS.

panels.title: The marginal signal lamp
panels.desc: On a warship's bow at night, a signal brazier gutters dimly in sea spray; two lookouts argue over whether it signals bright or dark.
panels.scene: Night on the prow of a trireme plunging through dark swells. At the bow post, an iron signal brazier flickers weakly, its charcoal half-drowned by sea spray and giving off only a faint, ambiguous orange ember. Two lookouts in woolen sea cloaks lean in: one points toward the fleet shouting 'Signal lit!', while the other fiercely shakes his head shouting 'Extinguished!'!
panels.caption: NO TIMBER OR RIGGING CAN SAVE YOU: A FAILING BRAZIER CAN LOOK LIT TO ONE LOOKOUT AND DARK TO ANOTHER.
